recommendation: Keep this audit as-is. Do not add a Condition refuted exception to clinicalStatus unless Patient Care explicitly revisits FHIR-29409; AllergyIntolerance and the shared refuted-record guidance need no FHIR-28458 follow-up.
issue_request: FHIR-28458 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request for R5 asking AllergyIntolerance and Condition to add guidance that clinicalStatus can be empty when verificationStatus is refuted, remove Condition con-5 and AllergyIntolerance ait-1, clarify both verificationStatus definitions as applying to the resource itself, and add refuted-record guidance.
initial_application: Git commit 54c9fc124088d2698ee846b31d29652a659158c1 applied J#28458 to the then-authoritative Condition and AllergyIntolerance spreadsheets and notes. The commit removed the relevant invariant ties, added J#28458 committee notes, updated verificationStatus definition text, and added legal-retention/no-longer-clinically-relevant guidance for refuted records.
additional_context: Condition and AllergyIntolerance are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current AllergyIntolerance still has clinicalStatus 0..1 and contains the FHIR-28458 verificationStatus and refuted-note text. Current Condition retains the FHIR-28458 verificationStatus definition and refuted-note text, but later Published issue FHIR-29409 made Condition.clinicalStatus 1..1 because it is a modifier element; that later decision is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-54914 later replaced only the Condition.verificationStatus comment and preserved the FHIR-28458 definition.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the obsolete con-5 and ait-1 constraints are absent, the applicable guidance is present, and Condition clinicalStatus cardinality is governed by a later formal decision rather than by an unapplied FHIR-28458 hunk.
